about: R5, research studio (curriculum v2 §11): verification, validation and reproducibility on one small study. Prairie Town is fictional; its plants, costs and battery are illustrative. Demand, wind and solar follow the real hourly shapes of 19 and 20 August and 3 September 2025 on the Southwest Power Pool grid (town_year.json, EIA-930), scaled to the town as in lesson 0. The benchmark day is made up. Every number the page states comes from the model in assets/learn/r05-build-validate.js; _tests/learn/test_r05-build-validate.js solves every run with the vendored HiGHS and writes `ref`, the precomputed results the page shows if the solver cannot load.
task: a one-page verification log for a model or a data analysis: each check with its result, one benchmark against a known case, one validation against measured data or an independent reference, and a rerun from a clean [[clone|clone]].
this page's battery study (the notebook has all five versions), or your own project.
Trustworthy analysis reaches Proficient: reruns from a clean clone (or a complete audit trail); verification log; one validation against real data or an independent reference.
taskTime: About 35 minutes guided here, then about 2 hours on your own: the notebook, Git and your log.
three: does the code solve its equations as written?
do the equations describe the real system well enough for the claim?
can someone else get the same numbers from a clean copy?

study.question: How much would a 50 MW, 200 MWh battery have saved Prairie Town on Wednesday 20 August 2025?
study.dataNote: Demand, wind and solar: the real hourly shapes of 20 August 2025 on the Southwest Power Pool grid (EIA-930), scaled to Prairie Town as in lesson 0. The plants, costs and battery are illustrative.

bench.label: a made-up day: 220 MW in every hour except 330 MW from 12:00 to 17:00, no wind or solar

checks.label: Units and sizes
checks.text: Every input in the model's units; every result within its physical size.

checks.label: Balance and signs
checks.text: Each hour balances, and stored energy falls when the battery feeds the town.

rules.name: Balance
rules.words: Plants + battery discharge − battery charge + unserved = demand, every hour.

rules.name: Stored energy
rules.words: Stored now = stored an hour ago + 0.85 × charge − discharge (MWh).

rules.name: Gas ramp
rules.words: The combined-cycle plant changes by at most 40 MW an hour, from 115 MW.

rules.name: End of day
rules.words: The battery ends the day with the 100 MWh it started with.

rules.name: Sizes
rules.words: Each plant within its size and the weather; battery 0–50 MW, 0–200 MWh.

symptoms: Most energy stored (the battery holds 200 MWh)

line.before: E = 200_000      # battery energy, from the spec sheet
line.after: E = 200          # battery energy, MWh (the sheet says 200,000 kWh)

bugs.right: Right. The battery holds more than its size: the energy limit was typed in kWh into a model that counts MWh.
bugs.wrong: That check passes here. Compare each result with its physical size first.
bugs.fixed: Fixed: **{ok}**, and stored energy never passes 200 MWh.

symptoms: Hours charging and discharging at once
Net energy to the town, as the balance rows count it
Stored energy at the end of the day

line.after: supply[t] += d[t] - c[t]   # battery: discharge feeds the town

bugs.right: Right. Charging was counted as supply, so the battery fed the town while filling up: energy from nowhere.
bugs.wrong: That check passes here. Follow the battery through one hour: where does its energy go?
bugs.fixed: Fixed: **{ok}**. The battery now charges when the gas plant has room and discharges in the hours the peaker would run.

symptoms: Stored energy, start and end of the day

line.before: # (no rule for the end of the day)
line.after: m.add(e[23] == E0)   # end the day with what it started with

bugs.right: Right. The 100 MWh the battery started with cost nothing in the model, and it sold them in the evening.
bugs.wrong: That check passes here. Compare what the battery holds at the start and at the end.
bugs.fixed: Fixed: **{ok}**. The gap, **{lunchGain}**, is the starting 100 MWh at the peaker's $100/MWh.
bugs.alsoText: Also right: the end-of-day rule has no row in the code. Closure catches the same bug from the results alone.

symptoms: Gas plant's biggest change in an hour, in this solution (limit 40)

line.after: for t in T: m.add(-40 <= cc[t] - cc_prev[t] <= 40)   # gas ramp

bugs.right: Right. The formulation has {rampRows} ramp rows; the code has {rampRowsMissing}. Today the headline happens not to move.
bugs.wrong: That check passes here: the saving is the same as the fixed versions. Count each rule's rows in the code.
bugs.fixed: On **{lesson0Label}** the same code says the day without a battery costs **{l0missingBase}** instead of **{l0base}**, and that the battery saves **{l0missing}** instead of **{l0ok}**.

line.after:
plan = solve(day='2025-08-19')            # what was known the day before
result = run(day='2025-08-20', battery=plan)

bugs.right: Right. Planned the day before, the battery could not know 20 August's demand, wind and solar.
bugs.wrong: That check passes here. Ask what the operator knew when the schedule was set.
bugs.fixed: Planned on the day before (a persistence forecast) and then followed: **{honest}**, {honestShare}% of the {ok} that [[perfect-foresight|perfect foresight]] gives.

benchSaw: The benchmark catches versions 1, 2 and 3. **Version 4 passes**: on this day the ramp limit never binds, so leaving it out changes nothing. A benchmark tests only what it exercises.

why.balance: That is verification: it checks the code against its own equations.
why.bench: That is verification too: the hand answer comes from the same equations.
why.measured: Validation compares the model with the real system, here with measured data.
why.clone: That is reproducibility: the same numbers again, right or wrong.

validationText: The study assumed an 85% round trip, the value in NLR's 2025 ATB. Measured on the U.S. battery fleet, the average was 82% in 2019 (EIA). Run the study with the measured value.
validationSaw: **{eta82}** instead of **{ok}**: {eta82Change}% less, so this input does not change the conclusion. Validating the claim itself would need data the model did not use, such as a real battery's metered schedule.

options: The code reads a data file by a path on one laptop, and the file was never committed
A random seed was not fixed

why.solver: No: the error is a missing file, before any solve.
why.path: Yes: an absolute path and an uncommitted data file. The clean clone has neither.
why.seed: No: this model draws no random numbers.
why.git: No: Git keeps what was committed; this file never was.

fixes: A download script with the source's address, access date and [[checksum|checksum]], so the data can be rebuilt
Paths relative to the repository, never to one laptop
The environment pinned: Python, SciPy and its HiGHS version
A tag on the commit that made the reported numbers

reproSaw: The fresh clone now gives **{ok}**, the same as before. A rerun shows the number is reproducible; the checks above are what show it is right.

checklist: Every input in the model's units, with the unit written beside it.
Every result within its physical size and limits.
Each period balances; a store's energy falls when it feeds the system.
The end state matches the start, or the difference is valued.
Each rule's rows counted against the formulation.
Every input was known when the decision was made.
One case with a hand answer, matched.
One comparison with measured data or an independent reference, with its source.
A clean clone at a tagged commit, a pinned environment, the same numbers.
